en.text:
'MARSHAL IS NO MORE'

'Today at six o'clock, the Shogunate's liaison council announced the passing of His Highness Moriuji Ashikaga, Senior Third Rank, Lord General of the Six Guards.'

'When His Highness passed, why His Highness passed—on these matters no explanation whatsoever has been supplied. Only this much has been conveyed: His Highness Shirou Kuniuji, the late Lord General's eldest grandson, is to enter the main keep of Fudaraku Castle and conduct government affairs in his place.'

'Confusion prevails in every quarter. Kyoto conspiracy, occupation-force intrigue, revenge by Okabe remnants—rumours are arriving from all directions. The continuing closure of Hachimangu since the recent sword-offering pilgrimage is also being connected to the affair, although'

'no theory possesses anything that could properly be called evidence. Speculation remains speculation.'

'However, informed sources maintain that the Lord General was in unquestionably good health. If correct, this would make illness an unlikely explanation, and some human intervention in the passing must be suspected.'

'Meanwhile, following the announcement, the occupation forces' General Headquarters—'

ja.html:
〝元帥、薨去〟

〝本日六時、幕府申次衆より、正三位六衛大将領足利
護氏殿下の薨去が発表された〟

〝薨去の日時、また死因等について、説明は一切ない。
　普陀楽城本丸には護氏殿下の御嫡孫であらせられる
四郎邦氏殿下が入られ、政務を代行される予定である
との伝達があったのみである〟

〝混乱の渦中にある各界では、京都の陰謀、進駐軍の
暗躍、岡部の残党による復仇等々、様々な風説が飛び
交い、また先日の奉刀参拝以来の八幡宮封鎖との関連
も取り沙汰されているが〟

〝どの説も根拠というほどのものはなく、憶測の域を
出ていない〟

〝ただ消息筋の情報によれば大将領殿下の健常は全く
疑うべくもなかったとのことであり、これが正しいと
すると病死とは考えられず、薨去にはやはり人為的な
何事かが関与したものとみられる〟

〝また、この発表を受けた進駐軍総司令部では――〟

en.html:
To call him a man who complained excessively would not be fair.

Suppose, without warning, somebody removed his freedom to drink tea. Naturally he would be furious. But coffee? Coffee he could sacrifice. See the difference. Already, considerable tolerance.
If he heard that his younger wife was unfaithful, yes, the sword would come out. But visiting a theatre repeatedly because its leading actor was handsome? That much he could permit.

Ordinary human tolerance, he certainly possessed.
People around him might have supplied a slightly different opinion. Opinions differ. What to do.

He himself had no wish to keep complaining about every small-small daily inconvenience. He had the pride of a British gentleman, a knight belonging to an old tradition. This was not some newly opened dignity.

That pride told him to practice tolerance. The same pride told him to throw down his gauntlet when the oppression became unjust. Tolerance beyond its proper limit was servility only. A knight's honour could not be expected to crawl about in that condition.

If his revered father struck him in anger at some fault, he would accept the blow with tears.
If his beloved wife slapped him for his long absence, he would answer with an embrace.

But a robber loots your property, and now you must also pay the bastard's taxi fare home?
Kyun? For what service?
No. One knife in the back was the correct farewell gift. His generosity ended there.

Therefore, that he was right, he did not doubt at all.

ja.html:
彼を指して、殊更に不満の多い男であったとは言え
ないだろう。

　ある日突然紅茶を飲む自由を奪われたなら憤慨した
であろうが、紅茶ではなく珈琲なら我慢もしたろうし、
年下の妻が密通したと聞けば剣を抜くとしても、彼女
が美形俳優を戴く劇場へ足繁く通う位なら許容できた。

　人並み程度の寛容さは備えた男だったと言って良い。
　彼の周囲の人間はやや異なる意見を示したかもしれ
ないが、それは必然的な見解の相違というものだ。

　少なくとも彼自身は、日々の些細なあれこれについ
ていちいち不満を述べ立てたいなどと思ってはいない。
　伝統ある<ruby>英国騎士<rt>ジェントリ</rt></ruby>としての自負というものがある。

　だがその自負は寛容を心掛ける事と同時に、不当な
弾圧に対しては手袋を投げつける事をも命じていた。
　度の過ぎた寛容の精神は単に卑屈であって、騎士の
名誉とは決してそぐわないからだ。

　敬してやまぬ父親が彼の過ちに怒り、鉄拳を振るう
なら涙と共に受け入れよう。
　愛してやまぬ妻が彼の長い不在を嘆き、平手打ちを
見舞うなら抱擁で応えよう。

　しかし彼の財産を略奪した盗賊に帰りのタクシー代
まで世話してやる<ruby>謂<rt>いわ</rt></ruby>れがあろうか？
　あるはずはない。盗賊の背中に贈るべきはナイフの
一投、それに尽きる。

　だから彼は、自分の正しさを全く疑わなかった。

en.html:
Cobden"Hurry! What is this dawdling!"
Accomplice A"...Patrol won't come for a while. Regulations say one round of the base every fifteen minutes. But on those fellows' watches, the second hand must do four rounds before the minute hand agrees to move."
Accomplice B"Must've dropped them in that sea. Rust, sir. Rust is doing the timekeeping."
Cobden"Bas, enough of this useless chatter! You are making me remember my Yokohama subordinates. I am becoming irritated."
Cobden"Finish it quickly... This sea wind is entering my bones. I want to return to my room and put a blanket over myself."
Accomplice B"Same ambition here, sir."
Accomplice A"...We should really do this? If it comes out, they won't just throw us out of the army and leave it there."
Cobden"Hmph. How will it come out? One patrol an hour. This information came from you only."
Cobden"A Rokuhara spy, some vandal doing mischief for enjoyment—any fellow who wants to enter can enter, no? Why specially suspect the men inside?"
Accomplice B"Well... haan?"
Accomplice A"Unless they catch us here, actually planting the explosives..."
Cobden"Therefore I am saying HURRY."
Accomplice A"Yes, yes."
Accomplice B"Too late to say no now. We'll do it. ...Only, the risk is beginning to look bigger than the payment."
Cobden"Enough to buy a whole ranch outside the capital, London. Even that is not enough?"
Accomplice B"Not saying it's small."
Accomplice A"Just, continuing in the army with this hanging over us..."
Cobden"What great love have you for the army? Retire when the chance comes. I shall do the same."
Cobden"Every day in this foreign country, looking at this dreary sea... Enough. Enough has become more than enough. Have mercy on me. The money is obtained. Now I want only to go home as soon as possible and live peacefully with my wife."
Cobden"Yes, and that is exactly what I shall do. What is wrong in that, you bloody bastards at Yokohama headquarters!"
Cannon"...Nothing. If that alone were your activity, even we bloody bastards would have no objection."

コブデン「急げ！　もたもたするな」
共犯Ａ「……巡回はしばらく来ませんよ。 　十五分ごとに基地をひと回りする決まりに なっちゃいますが、あいつらの時計は秒針が 四周しないと分針が進まない仕組みですから」
共犯Ｂ「そこの海に落として錆びつかせちまったん でしょうね。きっと」
コブデン「下らんお喋りはいい！ 　横浜にいた頃の部下を思い出して苛々する」
コブデン「さっさと済ませてくれ……。 　潮風が身に染みる。部屋に戻って毛布でも かぶりたい」
共犯Ｂ「そりゃ、俺達だって同じですがね」
共犯Ａ「……本当にやっちまっていいんですか？ 　バレたら軍籍剥奪程度じゃ済まねえだろ、 これ」
コブデン「ふん。ばれるものか。 　巡回が一時間に一度しか来ないと言ったの はお前達だぞ」
コブデン「六波羅の間者から単なる愉快犯まで、入る 気になれば誰でも入れるということだろうが？ 　内部の人間が殊更に疑われたりはしない」
共犯Ｂ「まぁ……ねぇ？」
共犯Ａ「こうやって爆薬仕掛けてる現場を押さえら れなければ、ね……」
コブデン「だから急げと言っている」
共犯Ａ「へい、へい」
共犯Ｂ「今更ナシにもできませんから、やりますが。 　……どうも割りに合わねぇ気がしてきたな」
コブデン「首都ロンドンの郊外に牧場を一つ買える程度の報酬 では不足か？」
共犯Ｂ「不足ってこともないですが」
共犯Ａ「脛に傷を持ったまま軍隊で生きていくこと を考えますとね」
コブデン「軍に格別の愛着があるわけでもあるまい？ 折を見て退役してしまえ。 　私もそうする」
コブデン「こんな異国で鄙びた海を見続ける毎日など もう御免だ。もう充分だ。もう勘弁してくれ。 　金は手に入れたんだ。後は一日も早く本国 へ戻って妻と平穏に暮らす以外に望みもない」
コブデン「ああ、だから私はそうするともさ。 　そうして何が悪いというのだ？　司令部ヨコハマの 腐れ野郎ども！」
キャノン「……無論、貴官がただそうするだけなら、 別に不満は無いんだがね。 　我々、腐れ野郎どもとしても」

Cannon"Lieutenant Colonel Cobden. For some time, I have been thinking you require a little advice."
Cannon"Open and honourable conduct is a knight's virtue. A night thief has different requirements. ...You undertake a crime and hardly bother to hide it. What arrangement have you made inside your head?"
Cobden"Clive Cannon..."
Cannon"Still, your chivalry has allowed us to stop you just in time. How can I complain? While this honourable mood is continuing, surrender gracefully also."
Cannon"Most of your wishes should be fulfilled. Return home, yes. See your wife, yes. Pass your time in quiet and peace, that also."
Cannon"Speaking, moving your body, spending money—these facilities may no longer be available."
Cobden"................................"

キャノン「正々堂々たることは騎士の美徳であって、 夜盗の美徳ではない、と。 　……犯罪やろうってのにろくろく隠蔽工作 もしないんだからな。どういう神経なんだ？」

キャノン「まっ、貴官の騎士道精神のお陰でこうして 水際阻止が間に合ったんだから、文句言えた 筋合いじゃないがね。 　ついでだ、投降も潔く頼む」
キャノン「貴官の希望はおおむね叶えられるだろう。 　本国へは帰れる。奥方との対面もできる。 静かに平穏に過ごすことも」
キャノン「ただ、口を利くことと体を動かすことと金 を使うことはもうできなくなるかもしれない が」
コブデン「……………………」

He had been absolutely certain that he was right.
So, when reality was placed in front of him, accepting it was not a small matter.

A long time was required.
